tasks.description: In contents/docs/product-analytics/subscriptions.mdx, add a section documenting the new enabled/pause capability: users can toggle a subscription off (pause delivery without deleting) and back on from the subscription list and detail views; re-enabling triggers an immediate confirmation delivery. Note that disabled subscriptions are skipped by the scheduler and that test delivery returns an error (409) for disabled subscriptions, so users must re-enable first.

In contents/docs/product-analytics/subscriptions.mdx, document auto-disable behavior: when a subscription's delivery target becomes permanently invalid (e.g. the Slack integration is disconnected/removed, or the delivery channel is unsupported), the subscription is automatically disabled and the owner is emailed with the reason and a link to manage it. Explain that re-enabling is blocked until the underlying issue is fixed (e.g. reconnect Slack), and that re-enabling a subscription whose schedule has ended requires extending until_date or removing count.

branches.question: Where are subscriptions documented in the docs tree (API, delivery, Slack integration, pausing/disabling)?
Does existing subscription documentation describe the deleted/soft-delete vs enabled distinction or any pause behavior?
What does the Subscription model and serializer expose for enabled, and what are the auto-disable reasons/messages?
What user-facing behavior do the frontend toggle and test-delivery 409 produce?
What does the subscriptions.mdx page currently say about managing/deleting subscriptions and the list view, so we can place a pause/enable section correctly?
What exact user-facing copy does the frontend toggle and toast use (labels, success/failure messages) for pausing/resuming a subscription?
What does the disabled-subscription email tell the owner (reason text, re-enable instructions) that should be reflected in docs?
